title: TTHE: verification only after exposed failures
selection_protocol: Select using unlabeled traces from the evaluation batch; final correctness feedback is not exposed to adaptation.
narrative:
Setting and seed: A 60-problem hard LiveCodeBench subset supplies unlabeled adaptation traces. The revised source describes post-training-cutoff task construction; exposed examples are available but hidden test outcomes are not given to adaptation.

Reported evolution: The selected scaffold retains a low-cost solving path and adds verification and repair when public tests fail. Additional execution is thus conditional on an observed failure, rather than required for every problem.

Evidence and limits: The route is reported as retained. Adaptation and scoring use the same batch, making this a transductive result rather than a sealed generalization test. There is no individual-change ablation. The SWE empty-patch retry and DS-1000 tasks in the shared configuration do not establish additional LiveCodeBench mechanisms.

title: EvolveNet: separating library-specific and shared behavior
selection_protocol: Local evolution, server validation and held-out testing; the qualitative merge is not an isolated ablation.
narrative:
Setting and seed: DS-1000 experiments evolve local client programs and merge them into a shared harness around frozen models.

Reported evolution: The round-2 example keeps schema preanalysis inside the Pandas branch while moving broadly applicable execution retries into shared cross-library logic. The merge preserves the intended scope of each client specialization.

Evidence and limits: This is a reported merge discovery, not independently inspected final source; final retention remains unconfirmed. The protocol uses local feedback, server validation and held-out tests, but supplies no causal ablation of this merge. The Pandas-specific example does not establish a concrete discovery on SWE or LiveCodeBench, nor does a short seed alone identify a particular tool architecture.

title: TTHE: treating an empty patch as a rerun condition
selection_protocol: Select using unlabeled traces from the evaluation batch; final correctness feedback is not exposed to adaptation.
narrative:
Setting and seed: Test-time adaptation on a 40-task hard SWE-bench Verified slice begins with stock mini-swe-agent, whose first attempt can terminate with an empty patch.

Reported evolution: The adapted scaffold reruns an empty-patch attempt with explicit reproduce–localize–repair–retest instructions and increases the step budget during multiround search. The change converts an otherwise terminal outcome into a conditional recovery path.

Evidence and limits: The selected mechanism is reported as retained. Selection without gold labels and subsequent scoring use the same batch, so this is transductive adaptation rather than unseen-task generalization. The budget and instructions change together. LiveCodeBench's public-test mechanism is not assigned to SWE, and the example's small-patch constraint is not general repository-repair advice.

title: ModularRSI: correcting tool dispatch and completion state
selection_protocol: Review and sanity checks promote module variants; later traces compare three rollouts per version on the same evolution task.
narrative:
Setting and seed: An initial modular harness evolves on related tasks outside Terminal-Bench, then undergoes frozen evaluation on version 2.0. The separate Section 6.4 method comparison specifies Terminus-2 and does not establish that seed for every main experiment.

Reported evolution: In Appendix D.4's Go repair case, the initial dispatcher rejects multiline write_file input and sends it to the shell, producing a command-not-found error. The reported revision identifies write_file or edit_block by command name and sends the remaining payload to the editing helper. The paper reports promotion in generation 9 and unchanged multiline handling in generation 12. A separate loop update re-presents pending acceptance conditions when the agent signals completion without commands.

Evidence and limits: The later case retains all successes while mean interactions fall from 36 to 25 across three rollouts per version. Concurrent parser and other changes prevent isolated attribution. The earlier unpinned released-code observation is archived in v0.1.0; current source-code behavior was not re-audited.

title: RRSI: bounding audits and waiting behavior
selection_protocol: Accept on evolve-set gain and cost thresholds; separate held-out transfer from candidate acceptance.
narrative:
Setting and seed: Evolution uses all 89 Terminal-Bench 2.1 tasks, beginning with Terminus-2 before the reported bounded audit and polling guidance. This record concerns candidate R0-A only.

Reported evolution: R0-A adds a bounded completion audit and nonblocking polling guidance for long-running work. Both are jointly accepted at that iteration, modifying how the agent checks completion and waits for results.

Evidence and limits: Acceptance at R0 is documented, but survival in the final harness is unknown. The polling mechanism is guidance, not evidence of a scheduler rewrite. Rejected candidates are not included among the evolved features. SWE does not participate in selection, and this within-benchmark acceptance does not establish held-out generalization or separate effects for the two instructions.

title: AIDE²: search diversity and bounded experiment history
selection_protocol: Evaluate evolved whole-runtime checkpoints on independent transfer benchmarks.
narrative:
Setting and seed: MLE-bench Lite22 is a held-out transfer evaluation of AIDE85, evolved on external tasks. Its AIDE0 ancestor greedily selects the best candidate and accumulates full candidate histories during drafting and improvement.

Reported evolution: The retained runtime searches multiple strategy arms with periodic cross-arm forks. It summarizes initial and recent solutions, adds selected error signatures when bugs recur, catches nearly empty code and prompts generalization to unseen test data. Search can change strategy while retaining a strong candidate.

Evidence and limits: Mean private percentile rises from 0.678 ± 0.006 to 0.722 ± 0.011; errors are one standard error. End-of-run median prompt-size reduction reaches 7×. These are whole-runtime transfer results, not module ablations, and AIDE47 scores higher on this benchmark (0.730 ± 0.005). Lite22 never enters evolutionary selection. The ineffective ranking penalty, rejected ensembles and scoring-script repair are not retained task-runtime mechanisms in this account.

title: Evolved prover interfaces: from compilation to interactive control
selection_protocol: Evaluate and reject unsuccessful interface proposals; Lean cost/time comparisons use the common-solved subset.
narrative:
Seed and retained changes: Evolution starts from a Rocq MCP server exposing whole-file compilation. Retained additions include a persistent session with step/rollback/state interaction, a try tool that tests up to eight candidates and commits the first success, and error hints. A heavily used lemma-search proposal yields no accuracy gain and is rejected; exemplar retrieval is also rejected. File-manipulation and project-verification tools added for Phase 2 are supplied setup changes, not empirically selected mutations.

Outcome and limits: Held-out miniF2F-Rocq evaluation compares the resulting interface across four models. Its Lean port lowers cost/time per solve on a PutnamBench subset, but solves fewer problems than lean-lsp-mcp. Human setup and review remain; this is bounded interface evolution, not autonomous improvement of every system component.

title: HarnessX
selection_protocol: Search repeatedly evaluates the selected task pool; shipped edits are analyzed by affected-task hit-rate.
narrative:
Setting and seed: WebShop. Composable HarnessX web-task configuration.

Reported evolution: Reported prompt/configuration edits reduce search and pagination loops; advisory processors address navigation. The added color-matching tool has zero measured hit-rate in the reported run.

Evidence and limits: Search repeatedly evaluates the full selected task pool. Aggregate improvement and edit counts do not establish unseen-site transfer or the causal effect of one component. Here hit-rate means tasks flipped to success divided by predicted affected tasks; it does not measure tool invocation frequency.

title: HarnessPAI
selection_protocol: Keep the program fixed within a rollout; revise between rollouts from execution feedback.
narrative:
Setting and seed: LIBERO/Pro; RoboCasa; other embodied suites. Code-as-policy interface around fixed action primitives.

Reported evolution: Execution failures revise programs and become node-local skills. The retained align-object-to-basket-mouth skill diagnoses a 5.3 cm depth error caused by estimating the target from all basket-mask points. It changes basket_center_world to use medians of upper-rim points for both horizontal position and height, with an all-points fallback when fewer than five rim points remain. The existing placement servo is unchanged.

Evidence and limits: The program stays fixed within each rollout and evolves between rollouts. Post-training on collected expert trajectories is a separate weight-update experiment; the published skill is not an isolated causal ablation.

title: VideoEvolve
selection_protocol: Instruction and full-harness configurations compared on the illustrated queries.
narrative:
Setting and seed: Charades-STA; ActivityNet; QVHighlights; ReXTime; TimeLens-Bench. The seed predicts one interval from 64 uniform frames and generic instructions.

Reported evolution: Instructions check repeated occurrences and event boundaries. Coarse sampling or unusual interval length triggers another prediction; substantial disagreement triggers a third. Start and end times are separately combined by medians.

Evidence and limits: All compared configurations use the same 64 frames; extra calls add computation. Figure 3 shows a recovered kettle interval. For the light switch, the instruction-only variant already moves the correct seed interval [0,1] to [1,3]; the three-call variant returns [1,4]. Extra calls therefore do not recover this instruction-level regression. These are cases; Table 3 separates code and instruction contributions across settings.

title: MemSkill
selection_protocol: Compare stabilized tail rewards across training cycles; roll back the skill bank after unsuccessful cycles.
narrative:
Mechanism: A fixed designer revises memory-processing skills from difficult cases while reinforcement learning trains their selection controller.

Evidence and limits: Removing the designer or learned controller lowers reported LoCoMo performance; the effects concern the complete ablated component. The controller is trained. This is not an entirely weight-free system or proof of retention under an arbitrary lifelong stream.

title: ERSkill
selection_protocol: Retain candidate skills using rollout-based frontier comparisons; train the router with soft reward targets.
narrative:
Mechanism: Evolves executable retrieval skills and trains a router from rollout rewards, maintaining separate capability and deployment frontiers.

Evidence and limits: The marked LongMemEval evaluation transfers ERSkill trained on LoCoMo without target-dataset training. Transfer concerns memory QA under the reported settings; the trained router and fixed retrieval primitives bound the claim.

title: SESA
selection_protocol: Failure distillation and frontier shaping feed later self-play; evaluate the resulting policy with memory on and off.
narrative:
Mechanism: Distills self-play failures into a bounded skill bank accessible to the solver, while policy learning updates the solver.

Evidence and limits: Removing failure distillation lowers the seven-benchmark mean by 2.7 points in the reported ablation. The mean is not a HotpotQA-specific effect. Skill-mediated policy learning and inference-time memory are distinct.

title: MaD-RSI
selection_protocol: General-task search uses three rounds and two candidate slots per round; two temperatures and two repetitions collect evidence.
narrative:
Mechanism: Uses disagreements among frozen executors on matched queries to guide shared harness proposals.

Evidence and limits: Expanded evaluation adds two models outside the four-model development population; coverage and joint success are separately reported. Not every metric improves: expanded safety utility coverage decreases. The study is preliminary and does not establish uniform model portability.

title: SERA
selection_protocol: Development and fresh-validation checks can admit revisions, but a budget-exhaustion fallback can also retain a development improvement.
narrative:
Mechanism: Revises planning guidance, progress criteria and execution-control rules from robotic execution failures.

Evidence and limits: Reported overall success increases from 44.38% to 51.38%. The aggregate includes fallback selections; it is not a fresh-validation-only estimate. A failure-only panel cannot measure retention of earlier successes.

title: RiseHarness
selection_protocol: Screen candidates, then require complete repeated development runs and improved aggregate pass rate; behavioral checks are optional.
narrative:
Mechanism: Uses agent trajectories and internal harness traces to propose executor-specific interaction changes.

Evidence and limits: Cross-benchmark transfer keeps the executor fixed; swapping final harnesses between models performs below their own-adapted references. Benchmark transfer does not imply executor portability. This is a full-harness comparison with noisy adaptive selection.

title: OO-Harness
selection_protocol: Accept subclasses for task clusters; freeze hierarchy and lessons before testing. Routing cannot inspect held-out grader feedback.
narrative:
Mechanism: Builds inherited harness subclasses and retains lessons for routing among specialized and base harnesses.

Evidence and limits: The disjoint-application-family experiment routes every test task to Base, preserving base performance. Fallback preservation does not demonstrate transfer of the specialized subclasses. Routing ablations are single runs.

title: HERD
selection_protocol: Commit a candidate skill registry only if it lowers verified-answer residuals; constrain distillation with prior-checkpoint and base-model anchors.
narrative:
Mechanism: Evolves textual skills, distills privileged teacher behavior into LoRA adapters, and merges them into the task model.

Evidence and limits: Reported forgetting is low, but the general-capability test still loses 6.3 points. Deployment uses changed weights; the skill writer stays fixed. Evidence is one model and one 25-stage stream.

title: BEAM
selection_protocol: Retrieve candidate memories, sample utility beliefs, and update the value estimator from execution and counterfactual feedback.
narrative:
Mechanism: Uses a LoRA-adapted, context-conditioned estimator of memory utility with evidence-driven updates and uncertainty-aware selection.

Evidence and limits: MATH-500 initialization improves reported AIME stream performance relative to training the value model from scratch. AIME adaptation continues; this is not unchanged zero-shot transfer. Stream improvement alone does not measure forgetting of earlier tasks.

title: VeriEvolve
selection_protocol: Use external-verifier agreement for evaluator admission and calibration; retain regression cases for later revisions.
narrative:
Mechanism: Constructs executable evaluators, freezes them within workflow search, then repairs them between searches using counterfactual states.

Evidence and limits: On 30 Filesystem tasks, GLM-5.2 success increases from 6 to 18; agreement on later agent states is 113/122, not perfect. Generated-suite agreement is not held-out agreement. Search remains externally calibrated and lacks a matched-budget control isolating evaluator evolution.

title: The Trinity
selection_protocol: Validate worlds and harness revisions; route using public task context and verified experience. Evaluation skills are prepared separately.
narrative:
Mechanism: Couples verified environment generation with inherited harness modules and capability-aware routing around a frozen backbone.

Evidence and limits: Combining evolved modules and prepared skills raises reported Unseen mean from 37.45 to 53.53 at iteration 1. The combined result cannot be attributed to modules alone. Routing updates experience sequentially; it is not stateless independent evaluation.

title: Selm
selection_protocol: Generate candidates on training tasks, select libraries on a distinct selection split, and report held-out test performance.
narrative:
Mechanism: Maintains a bounded skill library through validated CRUD updates, utility-aware retrieval and retirement of ineffective skill names.

Evidence and limits: On SpreadsheetBench with Claude-Opus-4.6 and no host harness, removing the validation gate lowers accuracy from 56.5% to 42.5%. Retirement blocks exact names, not semantic duplicates. Cross-benchmark warm-start transfer is left for future work.

title: Harness Evolution Hits a Ceiling
selection_protocol: Use 48 development tasks for evolution, training and ablation decisions; reserve 72 tasks for reporting.
narrative:
Mechanism: Evolves a planning harness, then crosses seed/evolved harnesses with base/trained model weights to study which gains persist.

Evidence and limits: Evolved-harness gains partly survive under the original harness after adapter training, with different process/content trade-offs across model sizes. The ceiling is conditional on the tested search, models and planning benchmark; it is not a universal limit on harness optimization.

title: Harness-Delta Attribution
selection_protocol: Audit selected evolved systems and separately evaluate held-out transfer; retain raw attribution components.
narrative:
Mechanism: Compares evolved harnesses with compute-matched seeds and shortcut-neutralized variants.

Evidence and limits: Detected shortcuts and additional test-time compute explain substantial selected search-set gains. Detected overfitting is a lower bound and residual generalizable improvement an upper bound; these are not an exact causal decomposition or a representative field-wide rate.

title: Harness Scaling
selection_protocol: Use an 18-configuration training design from a 243-configuration space; evaluate unseen white-box and external black-box harnesses.
narrative:
Mechanism: Trains a policy across a structured subset of factorized harness configurations.

Evidence and limits: Structured multi-harness RL improves reported generalization to unseen execution configurations. The transferred object is a trained policy, not an unchanged harness transferred across frozen models. Harness diversity alone is not the full intervention.

title: HarnessAdapt-RL
selection_protocol: Evolve support from training trajectories and select using training-aware comparisons; training tasks are disjoint from evaluation.
narrative:
Mechanism: Couples policy training with evolving repair guidance, tools and execution hooks.

Evidence and limits: Reported gains depend on training with the evolving harness, rather than adding its final tools only at evaluation. Each configuration is trained once; repeated evaluation runs do not measure training-seed variability. Evidence is limited to software repair.

title: Are Self-Evolving Agents Continual Learners?
selection_protocol: Update on the active contiguous task block and probe effects on prior and unseen groups.
narrative:
Mechanism: Evaluates retrieval memory and global harness edits across topic, workflow, domain and compound task shifts.

Evidence and limits: Aggregate gains coexist with interference and forgetting; retrieval can localize updates yet collide on similar queries requiring different workflows. Results concern the tested methods and four streams. They do not prove that every memory mechanism fails continual learning.

title: Recoverability and Verifier Strength
selection_protocol: Compare saved-version rollback with regenerated undo and test the approval verifier against reference outcomes.
narrative:
Mechanism: Measures verifier agreement and restoration of prior behavior after prompt changes.

Evidence and limits: Saved-version restoration and regenerated undo behave differently; deployed changes can already affect tasks before rollback. Only prompt edits were tested end to end, and the small verifier-strength experiment does not establish a universal safety threshold.
